::: {.route-question}
Question for today: CellCo's coating is in control. Is it good enough for a customer who demands Cpk 1.33, and what would it cost to get there?
:::

## When readings remember the past {#autocorr}

::: {.two}
::: {}
A beta gauge scans the web every second. Consecutive readings are close because the oven, slurry and foil change slowly: the data are **autocorrelated**.

Lag-1 autocorrelation for CellCo's continuous readings: **0.7**.

Standard charts assume independent points. With autocorrelation, the moving range is small, so I-MR limits come out too narrow: about ±1.64 process standard deviations instead of ±3.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
About 10% of in-control points then fall outside the limits. Operators learn to ignore the alarms, and then miss the real ones.
:::

**Remedy.** Fit a time-series model, here AR(1): x~t~ = μ + φ(x~t−1~ − μ) + e~t~. Chart the residuals e~t~, which are independent if the model fits.
:::
:::

## See the false alarms {#ar-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="arx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Lag-1 autocorrelation φ <strong id="arx-pv">0.70</strong><input type="range" id="arx-p" min="0" max="0.9" step="0.05" value="0.7"></label>
    <span class="w-toggle" role="group" aria-label="What to chart"><button type="button" data-m="0" aria-pressed="true">Raw readings</button><button type="button" data-m="1" aria-pressed="false">AR(1) residuals</button></span>
  </div>
  <svg id="arx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 250" role="img" aria-label="Individuals chart of 300 in-control readings"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="arx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('arx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  let s = 12345; const u = () => { s = (s * 16807) % 2147483647; return s / 2147483647; };
  const N = 300, z = []; for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 2) { const a = Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u())), b = 2 * Math.PI * u(); z.push(a * Math.cos(b), a * Math.sin(b)); }
  let mode = 0;
  function draw() {
    const phi = +document.getElementById('arx-p').value; document.getElementById('arx-pv').textContent = phi.toFixed(2);
    const x = [z[0]]; for (let t = 1; t < N; t++) x.push(phi * x[t - 1] + Math.sqrt(1 - phi * phi) * z[t]);
    const v = mode ? x.slice(1).map((q, t) => q - phi * x[t]) : x;
    const mu = v.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / v.length; let mr = 0; for (let t = 1; t < v.length; t++) mr += Math.abs(v[t] - v[t - 1]); mr /= v.length - 1;
    const lim = 3 * mr / 1.128, out = v.filter((q) => Math.abs(q - mu) > lim).length;
    const W = 1160, H = 250, L = 50, R = 20, T = 10, B = 26, X = (i) => L + i / (v.length - 1) * (W - L - R), Y = (q) => T + (1 - (q + 4) / 8) * (H - T - B);
    let g = `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(mu)}" y2="${Y(mu)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(mu + lim)}" y2="${Y(mu + lim)}" stroke="#BE654C" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(mu - lim)}" y2="${Y(mu - lim)}" stroke="#BE654C" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>`;
    let p = ''; v.forEach((q, i) => { p += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(i).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(q).toFixed(1); });
    g += `<path d="${p}" fill="none" stroke="${mode ? '#0F6E6B' : '#5A91BE'}" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    v.forEach((q, i) => { if (Math.abs(q - mu) > lim) g += `<circle cx="${X(i)}" cy="${Y(q)}" r="4.5" fill="#BE654C"/>`; });
    document.getElementById('arx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('arx-out').innerHTML = `${mode ? 'Residuals' : 'Raw readings'}: limits at ±${(lim / (mode ? Math.sqrt(1 - phi * phi) : 1)).toFixed(2)} ${mode ? 'residual' : 'process'} standard deviations; <span class="best">${out} of ${v.length} points (${(100 * out / v.length).toFixed(1)}%)</span> signal, although nothing has changed. An independent process gives about 0.3%.`;
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { root.querySelectorAll('[data-m]').forEach((q) => q.setAttribute('aria-pressed', q === b)); mode = +b.dataset.m; draw(); }));
  document.getElementById('arx-p').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[The process is in control throughout. Every red point is a false alarm.]{.hint}

## Charts for counts {#attributes}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**p chart: fraction defective.** Each lot of n = 500 cells; average defective fraction p̄ = 3.5%.

p̄ ± 3√(p̄(1 − p̄)/n) = 3.5% ± 2.47%

Limits **1.03% to 5.97%**. If lot sizes vary, the limits vary with n.
:::
::: {}
**c chart: defects per unit.** Pinholes counted on each 100 m² of electrode; average c̄ = 4.

c̄ ± 3√c̄ = 4 ± 6

Limits **0 to 10**. A roll with 11 or more pinholes signals.
:::
:::

[Attribute charts need far more data than variables charts to see the same shift. Measure the mass loading itself where you can; count defects where you cannot.]{.note-line}

## Break · 10 minutes {#break}

After the break: the process is in control. Is it capable?
:::

## Process capability {#capability}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**In control** means stable and predictable. **Capable** means the predictable output fits the specification. A process can be one without the other.

C~p~ = (USL − LSL) / 6σ = 1.2 / (6 × 0.172) = **1.16**

C~pk~ = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL) / 3σ = 0.55 / 0.516 = **1.07**

Out of specification: about **770 ppm**, almost all above 20.6.
:::
::: {}
**C~pk~ against P~pk~.** C~pk~ uses the within-subgroup σ (R̄/d~2~); P~pk~ uses the overall σ of all readings, which also includes drift between subgroups. An overall σ of 0.19 would give P~pk~ = 0.96.

**Normality.** ppm figures assume a normal distribution. Check with a histogram and a normal probability plot; tails matter most.

[Capability means nothing for a process out of control: its future output cannot be predicted.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Explore capability {#cap-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="cpx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Mean, mg/cm² <strong id="cpx-mv">20.05</strong><input type="range" id="cpx-m" min="19.8" max="20.3" step="0.01" value="20.05"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">σ, mg/cm² <strong id="cpx-sv">0.172</strong><input type="range" id="cpx-s" min="0.1" max="0.25" step="0.001" value="0.172"></label>
    <span class="w-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Preset"><button type="button" data-p="20.05,0.172">Today</button><button type="button" data-p="20.00,0.172">Re-centered</button><button type="button" data-p="20.00,0.150">Cpk 1.33</button></span>
  </div>
  <svg id="cpx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 230" role="img" aria-label="Distribution of mass loading against the specification limits"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="cpx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('cpx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  function erf(x) { const s = Math.sign(x); x = Math.abs(x); const t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x); return s * (1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x)); }
  const Phi = (z) => 0.5 * (1 + erf(z / Math.SQRT2)), LSL = 19.4, USL = 20.6;
  function tail(z) { // accurate upper tail for large z
    if (z < 5) return 1 - Phi(z); return Math.exp(-z * z / 2) / (z * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI));
  }
  function draw() {
    const m = +document.getElementById('cpx-m').value, s = +document.getElementById('cpx-s').value;
    document.getElementById('cpx-mv').textContent = m.toFixed(2); document.getElementById('cpx-sv').textContent = s.toFixed(3);
    const cp = (USL - LSL) / (6 * s), cpk = Math.min(USL - m, m - LSL) / (3 * s), ppm = 1e6 * (tail((USL - m) / s) + tail((m - LSL) / s));
    const W = 1160, H = 230, L = 40, R = 20, T = 10, B = 30, X = (v) => L + (v - 19.2) / 1.6 * (W - L - R), peak = 1 / (s * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)), Y = (d) => H - B - d / 4.2 * (H - T - B);
    let g = `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A"/>`;
    for (let v = 19.2; v <= 20.8 + 1e-9; v += 0.2) g += `<text x="${X(v)}" y="${H - 10}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">${v.toFixed(1)}</text>`;
    let p = '', out = ''; for (let k = 0; k <= 320; k++) { const v = 19.2 + k * 0.005, d = Math.exp(-0.5 * ((v - m) / s) ** 2) * peak; p += (k ? 'L' : 'M') + X(v).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(d).toFixed(1); }
    g += `<path d="${p} L${X(20.8)},${Y(0)} L${X(19.2)},${Y(0)} Z" fill="#0F6E6B" opacity="0.25"/><path d="${p}" fill="none" stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="3"/>`;
    for (const v of [LSL, USL]) g += `<line x1="${X(v)}" x2="${X(v)}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#BE654C" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="${X(v) + (v === LSL ? -6 : 6)}" y="${T + 16}" text-anchor="${v === LSL ? 'end' : 'start'}" font-size="15" fill="#BE654C">${v === LSL ? 'LSL 19.4' : 'USL 20.6'}</text>`;
    g += `<line x1="${X(20)}" x2="${X(20)}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#B9C1C6" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="${X(20) + 6}" y="${T + 16}" font-size="15" fill="#333F4A">target</text>`;
    document.getElementById('cpx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('cpx-out').innerHTML = `C<sub>p</sub> = <b>${cp.toFixed(2)}</b>, C<sub>pk</sub> = <b>${cpk.toFixed(2)}</b>, out of specification <span class="best">${ppm < 1 ? ppm.toFixed(2) : ppm.toFixed(0)} ppm</span>${cpk >= 1.333 - 1e-3 ? ', meets C<sub>pk</sub> 1.33' : ''}.`;
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-p]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { const [m, s] = b.dataset.p.split(','); document.getElementById('cpx-m').value = m; document.getElementById('cpx-s').value = s; draw(); }));
  root.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Re-centering alone cuts out-of-specification output by 37%, to about 485 ppm, at no change in variation. C~pk~ 1.33 also needs σ to fall 13%, to 0.150.]{.hint}

## Activity · Specification negotiation {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Paired groups · 25 minutes · agreed plan with ppm and cost]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
One group is CellCo (supplier); the other is a storage integrator (customer) who requires C~pk~ 1.33. Agree a plan, with who pays what.
:::

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Supplier's options**

- Re-center the die: one-time CNY 0.1 million.
- New slot die with closed-loop loading control, σ to 0.150: one-time CNY 1.2 million.
:::
::: {}
**Customer's costs**

Each 100 ppm out of specification costs the customer CNY 0.15 million a year in sorting and returns.

Each side may concede only with a number that supports it.
:::
:::

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: compute ppm, C~pk~ and the customer's annual cost for all four combinations before you go on.
:::

## Activity · Answer {#act1-answer}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Plan</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">σ</th><th class="num">C<sub>pk</sub></th><th class="num">ppm</th><th class="num">Customer cost per year</th><th class="num">One-time cost</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Do nothing</td><td class="num">20.05</td><td class="num">0.172</td><td class="num">1.07</td><td class="num">771</td><td class="num">1.16</td><td class="num">0</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Re-center</td><td class="num">20.00</td><td class="num">0.172</td><td class="num">1.16</td><td class="num">486</td><td class="num">0.73</td><td class="num">0.1</td></tr>
    <tr><td>New die only</td><td class="num">20.05</td><td class="num">0.150</td><td class="num">1.22</td><td class="num">130</td><td class="num">0.20</td><td class="num">1.2</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Both</td><td class="num">20.00</td><td class="num">0.150</td><td class="num hit">1.33</td><td class="num">63</td><td class="num">0.10</td><td class="num">1.3</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Only "both" meets C~pk~ 1.33. It saves the customer CNY 1.06 million a year against doing nothing, so a 1.3 million investment pays back in about 15 months. That saving is the customer's reason to share the cost. Re-centering is the obvious first step at any price.
:::

[CNY million. Re-centering takes 0.05 mg/cm² off every cell, so it also saves cathode material.]{.note-line}

## Workshop W8 {#w8}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Task**

1. Fit an AR(1) model to 500 continuous readings and chart the residuals.
2. Build a p chart for 30 lots.
3. Compute C~p~, C~pk~ and ppm, and size the variation reduction needed for C~pk~ 1.33.
:::
::: {}
**Deliverables**

The residual chart, p chart, capability table and improvement target.

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
Autocorrelated data make standard limits too narrow: with φ = 0.7, about 10% false alarms. Chart model residuals instead.
:::
::: {.tk}
p and c charts monitor counts, but need more data than charts of measurements.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
In control is not capable. CellCo is at C~pk~ 1.07 and 770 ppm; re-centering plus a 13% cut in σ reaches 1.33 and 63 ppm.
:::
:::

[Session 18: quality metrics, the cost of poor quality, and the course wrap-up.]{.note-line}
